title: Training Note on the Claimed-Line Value in Cartwise Grocery Orders Limit-Review Claims
content:
## Training note: valuing the claimed line of a limit-review claim

Cartwise Grocery Orders values the line named in a customer's limit-review claim by comparing the billed unit price with the original unit price on that line.

**Rule.** The limit-review claim value depends on how the billed unit price compares with the original unit price on the claimed line: when the billed unit price is below the original unit price, the value is the original unit price times the billed units; when it is above, the value is the average of the two prices times the billed units; when they are equal, the line is not re-priced and the value is the line's billed charge. Each value is rounded to the cent.

### Questions answered

**Where do the two prices and the units come from?**
From the claimed line's billed line entry: the original unit price is the price of the product originally ordered, the billed unit price is the price actually billed, and the billed units are the quantity billed.

**When is the rounding done?**
Once, on the product of the price and the units, to the cent, half up. The average of the two prices is not rounded before it is multiplied.

**A line billed below its original price — what value does it carry?**
The original unit price times the billed units. Hypothetical: original 7.00, billed 6.50, 2 units; billed charge 13.00, value 14.00.

**A line billed above its original price?**
The average of the two prices times the billed units. Hypothetical: original 7.00, billed 7.60, 2 units; average 7.30, value 14.60.

**A line billed exactly at its original price?**
The value is the billed charge. Hypothetical: original and billed 7.00, 2 units; value 14.00.

**Does a one-cent difference count?**
Yes. Hypothetical: original 7.00, billed 7.01, 3 units; average 7.005 times 3 is 21.015, rounded to 21.02. Billed 6.99 instead gives 7.00 times 3, that is 21.00.
